title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
Waymo's autonomous vehicles were deployed in a city during an unplanned traffic event without sufficient battery capacity to remain idle in gridlock for extended periods. Multiple vehicles drained their batteries and required towing when holiday traffic created sustained congestion that the system had not been designed or tested to withstand. This is a failure of deployment scope: the vehicles were operating in an urban environment subject to occasional severe disruptions that predictably render battery-only systems immobile.

A human dispatcher monitoring battery levels and traffic conditions in real time could have proactively repositioned vehicles or advised them to relocate before gridlock trapped them. The system was also exposed to direct physical hazard when one vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks on the street, a scenario that would benefit from human override capability during public safety events. It is not established whether Waymo had monitoring systems that could have detected the traffic anomaly and responded before vehicles became stranded.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
Multiple Waymo autonomous vehicles had their batteries drain and required towing during severe traffic congestion in San Francisco on Saturday following Fourth of July fireworks celebrations near the Golden Gate Bridge. Videos verified by NBC News showed at least a dozen stationary Waymo vehicles, primarily Jaguar I-PACE models, lined up on streets. The company attributed the problem to major traffic disruptions, high traveler volume, and unplanned road closures that created unexpected congestion. Waymo's roadside assistance team worked to clear the stranded vehicles, and the company stated it is evaluating ways to improve resilience during major traffic disruptions.

One Waymo vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks someone had ignited on the street, though no injuries were reported. Witness Dave Guingona spent nearly two hours in standstill traffic and observed people yelling at the driverless Waymos. San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie's office announced plans to discuss Saturday's traffic situation with stakeholders to improve future experiences. This incident follows a December outage when over 100,000 customers lost power and some Waymo vehicles stalled at intersections with nonfunctioning traffic lights.
